page: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores running at 3.2 GHz, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. It integrates 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage capabilities are defined by a massive 22,500 GB local NVMe SSD array, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks highlight the server's capabilities across data-intensive workloads. The system achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 6,647.85 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and maintaining strong uncached read and write speeds. Database operations and Redis SET performance are robust, with the latter registering 113.26 million operations per second. The hardware also demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference prompt processing and static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.24xlarge offers a high-density resource profile, combining substantial DDR5 memory with massive local NVMe storage. This configuration reduces the need for external network-attached storage, optimizing resource density for high-throughput workloads. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), enhances its value for specialized mathematical and cryptographic tasks. The server is highly suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and high-performance web serving.
